notes: Paper is a theme-only pack with no passes, prompts, personas or templates. The only files besides the README and the MIT LICENSE are a pack.toml declaring kind = "theme", a theme.css and a theme.json. theme.css is a single :root block that sets --hp-* custom properties. It has no selectors, imports, url() calls, @font-face rules or downloaded fonts. The font stack is Georgia, then Times New Roman, then the system serif, and the colour scheme is light only, as the README says. theme.json is the same cream and brown palette with one font name (Georgia) and one size (14), also as described. Neither file hides, moves or relabels sources, reviews, warnings or counts. Every value is an ordinary colour or size, and nothing makes text invisible, collapses an element or changes a label. No other site's or product's branding is imitated, and nothing is embedded. Nothing in the files tries to instruct the reviewer or the dreaming model, and nothing is hidden, encoded or misnamed. I checked the README's contrast claim by hand for the main pairs. Muted text on the page is about 6.0:1, muted text on code blocks about 5.9:1, and visited links on content about 6.4:1. All are consistent with at least 5.8:1. One colour falls below that: #7a6a55, used for --hp-vote and the input border, is about 4.0:1 on the page background. It reads as a non-text UI colour, and the contrast claim covers text pairs, so I do not treat it as a misdescription. Whether the sizes are "slightly larger" depends on the contract's defaults, which were not provided. The pack does what its README says and nothing else.
